title: quantization-debug-scratchpad-int8-fp8-bf16-nan
content:
Context / goal:
- Personal scratchpad for the INT8/FP8/BF16 NaN/quality investigation we hit on the private deployment (customer X) inference pipeline. Capture commands run, logs/snippets, hypotheses, quick experiments and next steps.

Issue summary (short):
- After switching weight-only int8 and enabling activation quantization, some inference runs return NaN logits or produce garbage (perplexity skyrockets). Problem appears nondeterministic but reproducible with a small seed of inputs. Happens on A100 pods (CUDA 12) and locally on dev GPU.
- When switching to BF16 activations or FP16 fallback, behaviour improves but quality still can be off. Suspect scale/zero-point overflow or asymmetric per-tensor activation ranges causing extreme rescaling.

Quick repro (commands I used):
- baseline FP32 run (good):
  python -u run_infer.py --model /models/llama-13b.fp32 --device cuda:0 --batch 1 --input sample_prompt.txt

- int8 weight-only (bitsandbytes) (observed NaNs):
  python -u run_infer.py --model /models/llama-13b.int8 --device cuda:0 --use-bnb-int8 True --batch 1 --input sample_prompt.txt

- int8 + activation quant (fake quant hooks):
  python -u run_infer.py --model /models/llama-13b.int8 --quant-activations int8 --calib-dset small_calib.jsonl --batch 1 --device cuda:0

- export ONNX to inspect ranges:
  python -u export_onnx.py --model /models/llama-13b.fp32 --out tmp/llama.onnx --opset 14
  onnxruntime_test (ORT) run with debug:
  python -u ort_infer.py --model tmp/llama.onnx --debug-outputs tmp/ort_debug

Observed logs / error snippets (captured):
- stack trace (trunc):
  RuntimeError: CUDA error: device-side assert triggered
  ...
  tensor contains NaN at generation step 2

- printed tensor check: (after model.forward)
  >>> a = activations["layer_10.ffn_out"]
  >>> torch.isfinite(a).all() -> False
  >>> torch.isnan(a).sum().item() -> 37
  >>> a[torch.isnan(a)] -> tensor([nan, nan, nan, ...])

- ONNX initializer ranges: many weight tensors have max ~ 3.4e+38 after quantization export (suspicious).

What I tried so far (experiments + notes):
1) Reproduce deterministically
   - Fixed seeds (random, numpy, torch.cuda.manual_seed_all) -> reduces nondeterminism but NaNs still appear for specific input prompts.

2) Sanity-check calibration data
   - small_calib.jsonl was taken from production traces but may contain outliers (logs with extremely long sequences).
   - Trimmed calibration to 1k short sequences (<=128 tokens) -> fewer NaNs but still occasionally triggered.

3) Change calibration percentile / clipping strategy
   - Tried percentile-based clip at 99.9, 99.99, 99.999 (increasing to 99.999 reduced extremes but increased MSE).
   - KL-divergence vs MSE for activation histogram quantization: KL gave slightly better downstream quality in my quick eval.

4) Per-channel vs per-tensor
   - Weight per-channel quantization (int8) + activation per-tensor quant: baseline approach.
   - Forced per-channel activations (not supported in many libs) -> implemented fake per-channel scaling for linear outputs, saw reduction in NaNs but implementation is slow and brittle.

5) Symmetric vs asymmetric quantization
   - Symmetric (scale only) caused larger clipping for activations with positive skew -> asymmetric (scale + zero-point) improved numeric coverage in activations with nonzero mean.

6) Check accumulation paths & intermediate dtypes
   - Confirmed GEMM accumulation uses float32 in cuBLAS by default for float16 inputs on A100 (TF32 interference?).
   - Suspect we had an unintended int8 GEMM accumulating in int32 followed by rescale to float32; if rescale factor is tiny -> underflow to 0 -> softmax division by zero -> NaN.

7) Try BF16/FP16 fallbacks
   - Activations BF16 (keep weights int8): reduction in NaNs, but some perplexity degradation vs FP32.
   - Full FP16 run (no int8): quality close to FP32 on eval set. Suggests numeric instability lies in quantized-act path.

8) Inspect scale terms for extremely small/large values
   - Dumped activation scales: some layers have scale ~1e-7 post-calib -> when multiplied causes tiny outputs after dequantization.
   - Others have scale ~1e+3 -> leads to huge values which saturate subsequent ops. Both cause problems.

9) Check for uninitialized params / accidental in-place ops
   - Searched code for in-place operations that may violate quantized buffers; flagged a suspected in-place clamp in custom layernorm wrapper. Replaced with non-inplace -> no change.

10) BitsAndBytes config experiments
   - bnb.nn.Linear8bitLt with different compute_dtype: tried compute_dtype=torch.float32 vs torch.float16. float32 compute prevents NaNs in many runs.
   - However float32 compute removes much of the int8 speedup. Need compromise (e.g., selective float32 for problematic layers).

Hypotheses (ranked):
- H1: Calibration outliers produce extreme scales/zero-points that lead to under/overflow in dequantization -> NaNs after softmax or layernorm. (Most likely)
- H2: Some layers (FFN) produce activation distributions with heavy tails / skew -> symmetric per-tensor quant loses important dynamic range, leading to catastrophic scaling errors.
- H3: Mixed-precision accumulation/rescale order bug in our custom CUDA kernel / wrapper (rescale done in int32 with rounding) -> precision lost and NaNs.
- H4: ONNX export path for quantized model incorrectly sets initializer dtype/scale metadata -> ORT inference produces bogus quantization params.

Quick checks to validate hypotheses:
- For H1: run calib with robust outlier trimming, clip limits by percentile 99.999 and ensure min scale >= 1e-6. Monitor scale histogram per-layer.
- For H2: instrument per-layer histograms on live inference to detect heavy tails. If present, try asymm per-channel for the layer.
- For H3: run with torch.autograd.detect_anomaly and set environment to TORCH_USE_CUDA_DSA=1 for debug, also run with NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1. Rebuild custom kernels with sanitizers if necessary.
- For H4: export ONNX with quant metadata validation script (I added a script: tools/validate_onnx_quant_meta.py) and compare scales between PyTorch and exported file.

Next steps / TODO (actionable):
- [ ] Curate a robust calibration dataset (remove outliers, use <=128 token windows). Run full recalibration.
- [ ] Add guard in quantizer: enforce min_scale_threshold=1e-6 and max_scale_threshold=1e4 (log warnings if violated).
- [ ] Implement selective float32 compute for top 3 problematic layers (empirically find them by running with per-layer compute_dtype override).
- [ ] Add per-layer activation histogram logging in the runtime (lightweight sampling) for 24-48h on dedicated pod to collect stats.
- [ ] Run bitsandbytes compute_dtype=f32 experiment across full eval set to measure quality vs perf tradeoff (baseline FP32 quality target: delta PPL < 3%).
- [ ] Validate ONNX export and ORT runtime quant metadata consistency.
- [ ] If still failing, isolate to minimal reproducer and open kernel bug with cuBLAS / custom CUDA team.

Notes for follow-ups / miscellaneous snippets:
- Quick python snippet to locate NaN-producing layer:
  with torch.no_grad():
      for i,layer in enumerate(model.layers):
          out = layer(sample_input)
          if not torch.isfinite(out).all():
              print(f"NaN at layer {i}")
              break

- Dump activation scale summary command:
  python -u tools/dump_scales.py --model /models/llama-13b.int8 --out scales.csv --calib small_calib.jsonl

- Temporary mitigation for prod: enable activation BF16 for all layers (cost: slightly higher memory/compute, benefit: no NaNs observed in 2k sample runs).

References / past notes:
- See earlier ticket INC-2326 for similar NaN in 7B model (resolved by clipping percentiles).
- Prior convo w/ Marco: "some skewed FFN outputs need asymmetric quant" (Slack thread link in Confluence page above).

Bottom line / current status:
- Root cause not yet conclusively identified. Strong candidates are calibration outliers and quantization scheme (symmetric vs asymmetric) mismatches for skewed activations. BF16 activations are a pragmatic fallback for short-term mitigation. Next immediate step: re-run calibration with stricter outlier trimming + enforce min_scale, then re-evaluate.
